Indeed, for `n>=n_0` the two Gaussian model branches are controlled by that
external maximal theorem and parity modulation, while (9.1) of the handoff
controls the residual layers.  For the finitely many layers below `n_0`,
each ball average is an `ell^2` contraction and

\[
\left\|\sup_{\substack{n\in\mathbb N_0\\0\le n<n_0}}|M_{d,n}f|\right\|_2
\le \left(\sum_{\substack{n\in\mathbb N_0\\0\le n<n_0}}\|M_{d,n}f\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
\le \sqrt{n_0}\,\|f\|_2.
\]

Here `n_0` is an absolute integer and the empty supremum is zero.
The internal proof audit is recorded both in Section 10 of the handoff and in
`SMALL_ALPHA_GAUSSIAN_AUDIT.md`.

### II. Fixed critical window

`CRITICAL_GAUSSIAN_THEOREM.md` proves that, for every fixed
`0<a<b<infinity`,

\[
\left\|\sup_{\substack{n\in\mathbb N_0\\ad\le n\le bd}}
|M_{d,n}f|\right\|_2
\le C_{a,b}\|f\|_2.

mathematical_input: Let iota be any type and let F,G:iota -> complex numbers. Suppose |F(r)|=|G(r)| for every r. The pointwise suprema of their absolute values in [0,infinity] are equal. In the case this implements modulus preservation under a unit-modulus parity factor; that earlier pointwise identity is the direct input of this extract.

source_steps.text: For every r, the equality of real absolute values also gives equality of the same nonnegative quantities regarded in [0,infinity].
Apply congruence of the supremum to those pointwise equal extended nonnegative values. No finiteness or boundedness assumption is needed, including for an empty index type.
